Frampol Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Frampol, Poland

Not demolished. Frampol's Jewish cemetery, established just after the town's own founding before 1736, largely survived WWII intact — a notably rare outcome in this collection. In 1942, about 1,000 Jews murdered during Operation Reinhardt were buried in three mass graves here; after the war, however, the local non-Jewish population stripped the stone fence and most tombstones for construction material. The cemetery was fenced again in 1985, with a Holocaust memorial erected and the mass graves marked, and further restored in 2006 and 2016. Over 160 matzevot survive today, most fragmented, the oldest dated 1735 or 1736.
